answer: Each identity must hold one roster slot with a volunteer rescue service, verified by training records, a public roster, and callout logs. Teams cover reef shorelines and ridge trails, so a volunteer cannot be a fable invented on paper: training takes weeks, callouts arrive at night, and teammates notice a stranger who never shows. One slot backs one identity; a missed shift suspends it, a duplicate merges both, and a proven fake audits the team. A farm needs one trained, available person per fake, retained month after month, costing far more in time and scrutiny than one identity buys.
